 ## Proof
 
 **Given:** AC and the data in the Statement.

-2.1 The projected-limit theorem [F2] applies to this weak limit. If it denotes the limit by $\nu$, then for every continuous test on the compact sphere both $\nu$ and $\rho:=h^2(\mu_\infty)$ give the limit of the same integrals $\int fdh^2(\mu_t)$. Testing $f\equiv1$ shows that both have the same total mass $M$. If $M=0$, both finite nonnegative measures are zero. If $M>0$, then $\nu/M$ and $\rho/M$ are Borel probability measures with equal integrals against every bounded continuous test, so uniqueness of weak probability limits gives $\nu=\rho$. Viewed as a measure on $\mathbb R^d$, this limit globally minimizes $F$ over all finite nonnegative Borel measures, exactly as asserted by the theorem.
